title: Algebraic isomorphism extracted from a constant adic quotient realization
statement: Under the hypotheses of the constant quotient realization statement, a realized isomorphism determines an algebraic morphism between the two derived coefficient objects that is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tags 093J and 03Q3, the nonempty-chart stalk detection part

proof.text: Transport the realized isomorphism through the canonical completion quotient comparison and the inverse-image/constant-section comparison. Evaluate at the supplied point of the etale chart; the stalk of a constant quotient module is its coefficient module, so this evaluation gives an algebraic morphism. Exactness identifies the stalks of its kernel and cokernel with zero, and nonempty-chart constant-section detection forces the kernel and cokernel to vanish. Hence the extracted algebraic morphism is an isomorphism.

proof_origin.place: Tags 093J and 03Q3, the nonempty-chart stalk detection part

from.place: The nonempty-chart stalk detection step used to extract the algebraic isomorphism before applying the derived isomorphism criterion.

lean.statement:
theorem constantAdicQuotientRealization_iso_lift
    (X Y : Scheme.{u}) (g : Y ⟶ X)
    {A : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing A] (d : AdicCoefficientDatum A) (n : ℕ)
    (W : Y.Etale) (_w : W.left)
    (E F : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (AdicCompletion d.ideal A ⧸
      (d.ideal.map (algebraMap A (AdicCompletion d.ideal A))) ^ (n + 1))))
    (h : Nonempty ((constantAdicQuotientRealization (W.hom ≫ g) d n).obj E ≅
      (constantAdicQuotientRealization (W.hom ≫ g) d n).obj F)) :
    ∃ f : E ⟶ F, IsIso f
